patches.summary: Serialize each promoted command's set flags into the POST request body, keyed off cobra's Changed() so an explicit empty string is still sent while unset flags are omitted.
patches.reason: The generated promoted_*.go template built `body := map[string]any{}` and called c.Post(path, body) without ever copying the bound flag variables in, so every parameterized command (get-text, set-text, copy-pad, ...) sent an empty {} body and the API rejected it with 'padID is not a string' etc. No-arg endpoints were unaffected. Gating on Changed() rather than value != "" keeps legitimate empty-string operations (e.g. set-text --text "" to clear a pad) working.
patches.validated_outcome: go test ./internal/cli (TestPromotedSerializesFlagsIntoBody / TestPromotedOmitsUnsetFlags / TestPromotedKeepsExplicitEmptyFlags) plus a binary smoke test confirm set-text now sends {"padID":...,"text":...,"authorId":...}, set-text --text "" still sends "text":"", and unset optional flags stay out of the body; per-endpoint API casing (authorId vs authorID) is taken from spec.json.
patches.upstream_issue: https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/2607 (generator: registered flags never wired into the request on non-GET commands; Etherpad confirmed as a second affected API — needs body-sink wiring + spec-derived param casing)
